subject: Private deployment rights & audit/escrow requirements
messages:
From: Lina Torres <lina.torres@medsys.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medsys.com
Date: 2027-02-25T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private deployment license scope and escrow-like request

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. MedSys is preparing the procurement packet for our Controlled Deployments team. Before we engage legal, a couple of items we need clarified so we can move the order form/MSA forward: 

- Licensing/Deployment scope: we need explicit language allowing on-premises install (customer-managed) with production use and options for a limited number of named instances. Please confirm whether the Order Form + addendum can grant that.
- Audit & evidence: our security team asks for audit rights (annual, third-party) to verify runtime controls and KV handling. They also asked whether you offer any escrow-like protections (source escrow or runtime artifacts) to allow continuity if Redwoods' support ends.
- Key management: require ability to use our KMS and a documented KMS handoff process if needed.
- Deliverables: sample SOC 2 report, recent pen test summary, and a standard addendum redline we can share with our counsel.

Can you confirm what you can provide and an estimated timeline for legal redlines? Our procurement target for the PO submission is March 10.

Appreciate a quick response — copying procurement.

Best,
Lina
Director, IT Procurement
MedSys Health

Attachments: medsys_initial_requirements.pdf (1 page)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina.torres@medsys.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-25T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment license scope and escrow-like request

Hi Lina,

Thanks — this is clear and very actionable. Short answers up front: yes, we can support a customer-managed on-prem/VPC deployment under an Order Form + Private Deployment Addendum; we have options for named-instance limits; and we can provide SOC 2 attestation + a redacted pen test summary. We do not typically provide full source code escrow, but we have a few proven alternatives (detailed below).

Next steps I propose:
- Loop legal/security to prepare a first-pass redline to your MSA/addendum (cc'd).
- Sketch the practical options for escrow/continuity for procurement to review.
- Schedule a 30-min call with your security lead and our Head of Security (Neha) — can you propose 2 slots next week?

Options we typically offer in lieu of source escrow:
1) Attested runtime image + hash stored with a neutral escrow agent (runtime-only deposit)
2) Auditor access window (remote/onsite) under NDA for a third-party auditor to validate controls
3) Customer-managed key option + documented handback process for KMS keys and access logs

Laura — can your team draft a narrow addendum that: (a) limits copy/use to MedSys' production internal use, (b) defines audit rights with scope and cadence, and (c) describes acceptable continuity options (1–3 above)?

I can put together a short commercial impact note (how escrow/attested runtime affects price/SLA) once we have a proposed addendum.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-02-26T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment license scope and escrow-like request

Jonas / team,

I've attached a first-pass addendum redline (proposed_addendum_redline.docx) that tries to balance MedSys' continuity concerns with our IP/licensing model. High-level notes: 

- License scope: we can grant a perpetual (or term-limited as negotiated) non-transferable license to run the specified model artifacts on customer-managed infrastructure for internal business use only. No sublicensing or re-hosting for third parties.
- Audit: propose mutually agreed audit windows (once per 12 months, 2-week notice) with remote-first approach; on-site limited to remediation or high-risk findings. Auditor must execute our standard auditor NDA and only access runtime/environmental artifacts (not model weights or source).
- Escrow/continuity alternatives: we propose offering an "attested runtime image" deposit with a neutral escrow agent (runtime binary + attestations + execution script) plus an agreed release criteria (e.g., company insolvency or prolonged non-support). Full source escrow is an exception request and will require additional approvals and fees.
- KMS/key-handback: we can support customer-managed KMS with documented key rotation and a formal handback checklist; note this affects support scope and incident SLAs.

Questions for commercial: what pricing delta are we willing to accept for (A) attested-runtime deposit vs (B) source-escrow exception, and (C) expanded audit cadence? Karthik / Jonas — please weigh in.

Lina / MedSys: if your counsel can provide a redlined sample of the MSA/addendum, we can do a line-by-line and get to a mutually acceptable draft in ~4 business days. If MedSys prefers source escrow as a mandatory clause, we'll need to escalate to VP legal and finance.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_addendum_redline.docx (tracked changes)

From: Procurement <procurement@medsys.com>

Date: 2027-02-26T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment license scope and escrow-like request

Laura / Jonas,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed approach. MedSys' legal preference is still source escrow, but they said they will accept a pragmatic alternative if the following are included:

- Attested runtime image deposited with a neutral escrow agent with clear release triggers.
- Third-party auditor access (annual) limited to runtime and controls under an executed auditor NDA.
- A documented KMS handoff and a 60–90 day operational runbook the escrow agent can execute to bring a customer-managed instance online.

Please confirm the expected cost and any SLA impacts (e.g., support window changes) for the attested-runtime + escrow-agent option. Also loop Kyle Anderson (kyle.anderson@medsys.com) from their outside counsel (cc'd) — he'll coordinate the legal redlines on their side.

Procurement
MedSys Health
